name: Short-USD returns on scheduled FOMC days: out-of-sample check of Mueller, Tahbaz-Salehi and Vedolin (2017)
claim_tested: A portfolio that is short the U.S. dollar against other major currencies earns significantly higher returns on days with scheduled FOMC announcements than on other days (paper sample 1994-2013: simple short-USD strategy 10.77 bps on announcement days).
primary_period_reason: The paper's data end on 2013-12-31, so 2014 onwards was never used to find the effect
secondary_period_reason: Overlaps the paper's sample; a check that this data and method reproduce the effect's sign, not new evidence
currencies: EUR, GBP, AUD, NZD, JPY, CAD, CHF against USD (the paper's G10 set without NOK and SEK, which are not in the archive)
data: data/historical_1h_from_15m (complete hourly bars rebuilt from the 15M archive); spot prices only
daily_return: Log change between 4 pm New York time on the previous weekday and 4 pm New York time on the day (the paper's 4 pm ET convention); the 4 pm price is the close of the hourly bar opening at 3 pm ET. Days where either price is missing are dropped.
portfolio: Equal-weighted average over the seven currencies of the return from holding the foreign currency against USD (positive when USD weakens), in basis points

fomc_days.scheduled: Statement dates in data/news/fomc_statements.csv that are the last day of a regular meeting on the Federal Reserve's calendar pages, plus 2008-12-16, which the file lacks
fomc_days.note: Weekend statements (2010-05-09, 2020-03-15) affect the following Monday, which is excluded instead

interest_differential: Not included. It adds the same small daily carry to announcement and other days, so it does not change their difference; this is a spot-return test.
costs: Round-trip 1.5 pips per pair (stress 3 pips), converted to bps at the entry price and averaged over the portfolio, for holding the portfolio from 4 pm ET the day before to 4 pm ET on the FOMC day. Overnight swap is not modeled.
decomposition_info_only: From 2014 the statement is released at 2 pm ET: pre = 4 pm ET previous day to 2 pm ET; post = 2 pm to 4 pm ET, for FOMC and other days
statistics: Difference in means, FOMC minus other days: Welch t-statistic and a one-sided permutation p-value (20000 label shuffles within the period, seed 42)
success_criteria: Primary period: FOMC-day mean exceeds the other-day mean with one-sided permutation p <= 0.05
Primary period: FOMC-day mean after 1.5-pip round-trip costs > 0
The FOMC minus other-day difference is positive in both 2014-2019 and 2020-2026
use: Only if all criteria hold may the app show an informational FOMC-day note; it would not change any decision, ranking or gate
